title: Transport identifies the exchange map
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete commutative ring. Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f$ and $f'$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let $L\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. On each pro-etale corner use precisely the constant ring $R_T=\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$ and its module category [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]; use the canonical structure isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] on all four edges. Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], $l_u=u_{\Et}^{-1}$, $r_u=Ru_{\Et,*}$, $p_u=Lu_{\Proet}^*$, $s_u=Ru_{\Proet,*}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $a_u:A_Ul_u\xrightarrow{\sim}p_uA_V$ be the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and let $b_u:A_Vr_u\xrightarrow{\sim}s_uA_U$ for $u=f,f'$ be the canonical counit-mate comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], namely the transpose of $A_U\varepsilon_u^e\circ a_{u,r_u}^{-1}$. These are the specified direct-image comparison isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], with their normalization now made explicit.

Define
$$S_L=p_g(b_{f,L})\circ a_{g,r_fL}:A_{Y'}l_gr_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}p_gs_fA_XL,$$
$$T_L=s_{f'}(a_{g',L})\circ b_{f',l_{g'}L}:A_{Y'}r_{f'}l_{g'}L\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{f'}p_{g'}A_XL.$$
Let $E_L$ be the etale module exchange, the unit--square--counit mate of $\theta^e_\square:l_{f'}l_g\cong l_{g'}l_f$, using the module version of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] as identified by [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-exchange-compatibility]. Then
$$T_L\circ A_{Y'}(E_L)=\Ex^{R}_{\square,A_XL}\circ S_L,$$
where $\Ex^R$ is precisely the ambient ringed unit--counit exchange of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. Under the constant-ring identifications its source and target are $g_{\Proet}^{-1}Rf_{\Proet,*}A_XL$ and $Rf'_{\Proet,*}g'_{\Proet}{}^{-1}A_XL$, respectively. Thus conjugation by $S_L,T_L$ identifies the specified etale exchange with the specified pro-etale exchange.

proof.text: Apply comparison_counit to both vertical edges, and comparison_square to the pullback square. A private categorical transport lemma transposes both exchange composites under the bottom pro-etale adjunction, precomposes with the invertible vertical pullback comparison, and uses naturality to move the direct-image target comparison through the counit. The two mateEquiv_counit identities identify the remaining transposes. Square coherence then rewrites one route into the other; the first vertical counit equation closes the calculation. Injectivity of the adjunction hom-equivalence and cancellation of the comparison isomorphism give the equality. Specialize the generic lemma to the exact Plus-to-unbounded comparison functors and unfold only the endpoint comparisons and the fixed Etale.baseChange unit-square-counit formula. The counit and square lemmas are provided by lower Core modules in namespace AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.ComparisonCore, with the fixed comparisons expanded to their unchanged defining formulas. This avoids importing the post-sync upstream module from a proof dependency. The generic transport helper remains private in the upstream module.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. For a cartesian square
[def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] in which $f$ and $f'$ are quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, and $L\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, use the natural comparison isomorphisms

$$
 \nu_{X'}^*g'_{\Et}{}^{-1}\simeq
 g'_{\Proet}{}^{-1}\nu_X^*,
 \qquad
 \nu_Y^*Rf_{\Et,*}L\simeq Rf_{\Proet,*}\nu_X^*L,
$$

and their analogues for the other sides. Conjugating the etale exchange map
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] by these isomorphisms gives the pro-etale
unit--counit exchange map

$$
 g_{\Proet}^{-1}Rf_{\Proet,*}\nu_X^*L
 \longrightarrow
 Rf'_{\Proet,*}g_{\Proet}'{}^{-1}\nu_X^*L
$$

of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange].

proof.text:
Expanding the unit--$\theta_\square$--counit composite of
[def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] and conjugating each arrow through the
comparison isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] (the latter applies to $f$ and $f'$,
which are quasi-compact and quasi-separated) gives exactly the mate of the ambient
ringed exchange; naturality of the two comparison adjunctions makes the
resulting square commute.
